description:
Real ownership. Real impact. Build from day one.

Are you an ambitious graduate ready to tackle complex, real-world challenges at the intersection of data, strategy and tech? 

The Future Leaders Graduate Program – Business Analytics at Picnic is a one-year launchpad for exceptional talents. From day one, you join a business team, own a business topic, and become an expert in your field.

At Picnic, we’re building the future of grocery. Using cutting-edge technology and data-driven innovation, we challenge the status quo and build the world’s smartest, most customer-focused supermarket.
We move fast, think big, and turn bold ideas into tangible impact.

Tricks of the trade

  • Lead with ambition: Bring your relentless determination, creativity, and grit. Take the driver’s seat and redefine the grocery shopping experience for millions. You will be expected to think independently, move fast, and deliver results.
  • Steep learning curve: Your growth comes from owning real problems, testing your ideas, learning from your mistakes and starting again. You'll blend hands-on training with immediate execution, you’ll move at a pace that accelerates your growth like nowhere else.
  • Solve real-life puzzles: Spot opportunities, use tools at the forefront of technology, and own the outcome end to end. Not just making slides, but building the solution yourself.
  • Innovate across borders: You’ll collaborate with teams across the Netherlands, Germany, and France, tackling challenges that redefine how Picnic operates at a European scale.
  • High-performance environment: You’ll work alongside some of the best teams in analytics and tech, people who set a high bar and expect you to do the same.

From learning to leading

Throughout this one-year program, you’ll own business-critical projects from start to finish right from the get-go, supported by mentorship, learning sessions, and regular feedback.

You’ll strengthen your leadership skills in project management, storytelling, stakeholder communication, and giving and receiving feedback, while sharpening your technical skills in Python, SQL, Excel, and PowerPoint.

As your scope grows, so does your responsibility. You might scale your initial project or take on new challenges within the same domain. Either way, there’s always a new challenge to lead and an opportunity to make an impact. That’s why every journey is unique: there’s no standardized path through the program, just continuous opportunities to grow and lead.

Where you’ll make an impact

From day one, you’ll be embedded in a business team, taking ownership in one of the following domains:

  • Consumer - Drive growth through pricing, supplier strategy, and our market strategy. Think: Shaping our successful market entry into new cities. Your decisions shape how millions of customers experience Picnic. 
  • Logistics - Build the backbone of Picnics operations. Think: robotic fulfilment, demand forecasting, route optimization across Europe and much more

Your superpowers

You don't wait for permission. You see a problem, build the solution, and bring people with you, before anyone asks. You've probably already started something: a project, a product, a business, an initiative that didn't exist until you made it happen.

More specifically, you:

  • Are about to graduate (or recently graduated) a Masters in a quantitative field: e.g., mathematics, econometrics, engineering, or similar
  • Have experience in high-performance environments: consulting, fast-growth startups, or competitive internships and know what it means to raise the bar
  • Show an entrepreneurial mindset: you build, improve, and take ownership without being asked
  • Think like a builder: hands-on, curious, and driven to challenge the status quo with practical solutions
  • You have already gained basic knowledge in PowerPoint, Python, SQL, Excel or alternative coding languages 
  • EU citizenship or valid EU working permit required.

Many strong candidates (particularly women) talk themselves out of applying because they don't tick every box. If this excites you and you believe you have what it takes, apply. We only hire when we find the right match. That’s why our selection process is intentionally highly selective.

 Why Picnic?

  • Grow as we grow. We’re scaling quickly across countries and millions of customers and this is just the start. Grow your impact as we grow; we invest in your path but the driver's seat is always yours
  • Work with other innovators. Work with a driven, energetic team that builds, wins, and celebrates together (think of legendary Friday drinks, our Ski trip and our parties)
  • Kickstart your career. Earn a competitive salary and step into a program designed to launch your long-term future at Picnic

Picnic Perks 

🏆 Rewarding Impact from Day One

You’ll receive an attractive compensation package, designed to reward your ambition, drive, and the direct impact you’ll make from your very first project.

🍎Learning & development 

Our Future Leaders Graduate Program - Business Analytics is designed to offer you a steep learning curve by taking business ownership and end-to-end responsibility early on. You’ll get to learn by doing, while mentored by our Picnic leaders that had a similar journey like you. Next to that, you’ll benefit from other opportunities like Lepaya training for polishing soft skills or Picnic Tech Academy training in case you want to learn new skills other than what you already do in this program. We also offer free access to trained psychologists via our OpenUp partner, and German language classes if you’d like to get your experience in Germany to the next level. 

🗺️Relocation

If you’re moving from another country to join Picnic we make it as smooth as possible for you. We’ll cover your flight costs and a first month's accommodation. 

 🥗Fresh Lunch, coffee, and snacks 

Our offices are equipped with fully-fledged coffee bars and a kitchen. We get delicious fresh and warm lunches every day so you can keep your energy up.

⛳All the rest 

At Picnic you get 30 holidays, we cover your travel expenses and offer a pension plan. We subsidise your Deutschlandticket and with the Lease-a-Bike you can get to work sustainably and healthily. And your phone and laptop are on us, of course.

FAQ

Do I need a quantitative background? It's a strong advantage, but not a hard requirement. If your internships and projects demonstrate real hands-on ownership and data-driven thinking, we'll consider your application. You do need a Master's degree, basic knowledge of Python or SQL, and relevant work experience.

Does the program include rotations? No, intentionally. We believe depth creates ownership, and ownership creates impact. Rather than rotating across teams, you’ll go deep in one area, build real expertise, and gradually expand your scope as your impact grows. If you have topic preferences, tell us during the process.

In what language should I apply? English. Please include your CV and Master's degree transcript or any other relevant test scores (e.g., GMAT)

What are the long-term opportunities after the program? This program is a fast track into a high-impact career at Picnic, it’s an entry point for a long-term future, not a two-year stopover. 

Career paths here are as varied as the people on them. Some grow vertically, building deep expertise and a team around them as their project expands. Others move laterally - from Commercial to Fulfilment, Distribution to Customer, or wherever their strengths and ambitions take them. What they share is real ownership, real impact, and a career they shaped themselves.

title: Commercial Director - Bern (m/f/d)

description:
Commercial(e) terrain indépendant(e) – SumUp

Vous avez une réelle expérience de la prospection à froid, sur le terrain ou par téléphone ? Rejoignez SumUp et accompagnez les commerçants avec des solutions de paiement simples et reconnues.

Vos missions

  • Prospecter les cafés, restaurants, boutiques, salons et entreprises de votre secteur ;
  • Identifier leurs besoins, présenter la solution adaptée et réaliser des démonstrations ;
  • Accompagner les commerçants jusqu’à l’activation et développer votre portefeuille.

La prospection est réalisée par vos soins : aucun portefeuille de leads n’est fourni.

Votre rémunération

Cette activité est rémunérée exclusivement à la commission, sans salaire fixe ni plafond :

  • 50 % de commission immédiate sur le matériel, les logiciels et les paiements générés par le commerçant au cours de son premier mois ;
  • 20 % de revenus récurrents sur l’activité de chaque commerçant signé, versés mensuellement pendant une durée pouvant aller jusqu’à 24 mois.

Exemple : un commerçant actif générant environ 15 000 € de volume de paiement mensuel peut vous permettre de percevoir plus de 1 000 € de commissions cumulées sur 24 mois.Ce montant indicatif varie selon les produits vendus, l’activation, le volume réel et le maintien de l’activité du commerçant. Aucun revenu minimum n’est garanti.

Vos outils et votre organisation

SumUp fournit une formation initiale, un terminal de démonstration et des supports commerciaux. Un référent de secteur reste disponible pour vous accompagner.

Votre zone est définie pendant le recrutement selon votre localisation et les secteurs ouverts. Vous organisez librement votre activité. Vos déplacements et les frais associés restent à votre charge ; aucun véhicule de fonction n’est fourni.

Votre profil

  • Au moins un an d’expérience en prospection à froid, terrain ou téléphonique, au cours des six dernières années ;
  • À l’aise dans une démarche commerciale proactive auprès de professionnels ;
  • Autonome, persévérant(e), fiable et orienté(e) résultats ;
  • Disponible au moins trois jours par semaine ;
  • Numéro SIRET valide au démarrage.

Processus de recrutement

  1. Échange téléphonique avec notre équipe recrutement ;
  2. Entretien avec le ou la référente de votre secteur ;
  3. Décision rapide fondée sur votre expérience et votre motivation.

Envie de développer votre activité avec une rémunération sans plafond et des revenus récurrents potentiels ? Postulez dès maintenant !

Job Application Tip

We recognise that candidates feel they need to meet 100% of the job criteria in order to apply for a job. Please note that this is only a guide. If you don’t tick every box, it’s ok too because it means you have room to learn and develop your career at SumUp.

description:
Conseiller(ère) commercial(e) terrain expérimenté(e) 

Indépendant | Rémunération à la commission uniquement | Territoire de vente local | Commissions déplafonnées

À propos de l’opportunité

Nous recherchons des commerciaux terrain expérimentés, à l’aise pour se rendre dans une entreprise, engager la conversation avec le propriétaire et convaincre de nouveaux commerçants.

En tant que conseiller commercial itinérant indépendant, vous vendrez les solutions de paiement, de point de vente et logicielles de SumUp aux petites et moyennes entreprises de votre région. Vous identifierez vous-même vos prospects, gérerez votre portefeuille d’opportunités et accompagnerez les clients lors de leur mise en route.

Vous devrez justifier d’une expérience en prospection à froid et apprécier la vente en face à face sur le terrain. Vous gérerez votre propre activité et organiserez vos démarches commerciales de manière autonome, tout en bénéficiant de la formation et du soutien de SumUp.

Vos missions

  • Trouver de nouveaux clients grâce à des visites en face à face, de la prospection en porte-à-porte et des démarches directes.

  • Cibler les entreprises locales générant d’importants volumes de paiement et susceptibles de tirer parti des produits SumUp.

  • Poser des questions sur le fonctionnement de chaque entreprise et recommander des solutions adaptées en matière de paiement, de matériel, de caisse et de logiciels.

  • Gérer le processus de vente depuis le premier échange, en passant par les démonstrations de produits, la gestion des objections et la conclusion, dans le cadre du partenariat.

  • Aider les clients à mettre en place et à commencer à utiliser leurs produits SumUp.

  • Établir des relations avec les chefs d’entreprise et demander des recommandations aux clients satisfaits.

  • Planifier vos visites et vos suivis afin d’optimiser votre temps sur le terrain.

  • Suivre votre activité, vos opportunités et vos résultats de vente, et transmettre les informations nécessaires au traitement des ventes.

  • Échanger avec votre interlocuteur SumUp pour bénéficier de son expertise produit et de conseils commerciaux.

Ce que nous recherchons

Indispensable

  • Au moins un an d’expérience dans la vente sur le terrain dans des secteurs tels que les télécommunications, l’énergie, les technologies d’entreprise, la gestion des déchets, les systèmes de sécurité ou l’approvisionnement en produits alimentaires et boissons.

  • Une expérience de la prospection à froid, notamment en démarchant des entreprises en face à face et en trouvant vos propres prospects.

  • Une expérience de la vente auprès de petites et moyennes entreprises et des relations directes avec les propriétaires ou les décideurs.

  • Des résultats démontrables en matière d’acquisition de nouveaux clients et d’atteinte d’objectifs commerciaux. Nous vous demanderons des exemples de vos réalisations et de la manière dont vous y êtes parvenu.

  • La capacité à gérer un processus de vente de la première prise de contact à la conclusion, y compris la gestion des questions et des objections.

  • Un bon sens de l’organisation et un suivi rigoureux.

  • La capacité à gérer les refus, à tirer les leçons des retours d’expérience et à persévérer.

  • Une bonne compréhension du statut d’indépendant et la volonté de développer votre portefeuille de clients.

  • La capacité à vous déplacer sur votre territoire de vente afin de rencontrer régulièrement vos prospects et clients.

Atouts

  • Un réseau existant de chefs d’entreprise locaux susceptibles de bénéficier des produits SumUp.

  • Une expérience dans le domaine des paiements, des services aux commerçants ou des systèmes de point de vente.

Une expérience de la vente par téléphone est un atout, mais vous devez également avoir vendu en face à face sur le terrain.

Rémunération

Il s’agit d’une activité indépendante, rémunérée exclusivement à la commission, sans salaire de base ni revenu minimum garanti. Les commissions sont déplafonnées et dépendent de vos résultats commerciaux et de l’activité des commerçants apportés.

Le système de commissions comprend, dans le cadre des conditions Partner :

  • Paiements : 50 % du revenu net annualisé lié aux transactions.

  • Matériel : 50 % du prix de vente retenu dans le barème.

  • Logiciels et abonnements : 50 % du montant annuel retenu dans le barème.

  • Revenu résiduel : 20 % du revenu net mensuel généré par les commerçants apportés, pendant une durée maximale de trois ans.

  • Avantage de bienvenue : trois fois le montant habituel des commissions résiduelles pendant les trois premiers mois.

  • Primes supplémentaires liées à certains produits ou opérations commerciales.

Les nouveaux partenaires bénéficient des conditions Partner pendant la période de lancement. Leur maintien est ensuite soumis aux critères d’activité du programme ; un barème Agent de 40 %, sans commissions résiduelles, peut s’appliquer.

Les conditions d’éligibilité, les bases de calcul et les modalités de versement sont précisées dans le contrat et présentées avant tout engagement. Les commissions s’entendent avant déduction de vos frais professionnels, cotisations sociales et impôts applicables.

Formation et accompagnement

Nous vous aiderons à vous familiariser avec les produits et leur commercialisation grâce à un parcours initial et à un accompagnement continu couvrant la prospection, les entretiens de vente, les démonstrations, la gestion des objections et l’accompagnement des clients.

Les modalités du parcours initial et les prérequis à la commercialisation vous seront communiqués avant le démarrage.

Votre interlocuteur SumUp vous apportera également son soutien en matière de développement territorial, d’analyse de vos opportunités et de conseils commerciaux, dans le respect de votre autonomie d’organisation.

  • Proven experience of user communication and education such as having been responsible for product documentation, blogs, written or video tutorials, presentations

description: Accelerating embodied AGI. The next ten years of AI will not be won in software. They will be won in the physical world: in factories, hospitals, kitchens, fields, and homes. The companies that own that data will own the century. MicroAGI is building it. We are a data research and deployment lab. Atlas captures the manual work inside Europe’s industrial champions, trains foundation models on it, and deploys the right robot onto the floor, with no teleoperation and no interruption to the line. Shift records how physical work actually happens and turns it into training-ready data. We were founded by former Formula 1 engineers from Red Bull Racing and Mercedes, together with a researcher from the Alan Turing Institute. Our $55M seed round, the largest in German history, was led by Hummingbird with Northzone, LocalGlobe, Village Global, and redalpine. We are based in Munich, with our research centre in Zürich and teams in London, New York, and Istanbul. We are now building the engineering and research teams that will take Atlas into new industries. Our models learn from data captured in the physical world, by hardware we design and build ourselves. As Head of Hardware, you own that hardware end to end: electrical, firmware, and the mechanical integration that holds it together, from the first schematic to devices running on factory floors. You lead the team that builds it. Today that is about six engineers on robotics, three on EMG sensing, and three on camera systems, plus contractors, and it will grow quickly. Our Electrical Engineer and Embedded Engineer roles report to you. You set the architecture they build against, and you still build alongside them. This is a founder-shaped role, not a management seat. We are looking for someone who has carried a product from a blank page to customers with real skin in the game, wants to build both the thing and the team that builds it, and would rather design than review. If that sounds like you, you will want to do it again at the earliest stage. What You Will Do Own the hardware roadmap for Shift and Atlas data capture: wearables, sensor rigs, camera systems, and prototype robots. What we build, in what order, and why. Set the system architecture across electrical, firmware, and mechanical: sensors, compute, power, wireless, and enclosures. Make the trade-offs, and make them stick when disciplines disagree. Stay on the bench: schematics, layout reviews, board bring-up, and a scope in your hands when the team is stuck. On the days it matters, you are the best electrical engineer in the room. Lead and grow the team: hire, set the bar, run design reviews, and give engineers ownership of whole subsystems rather than tickets. Guarantee data quality end to end: EMG and EEG front ends, camera pipelines, IMUs, and synchronization across many devices, so that what reaches the ML team is clean, time-aligned, and trustworthy. Take designs from prototype to small-batch production: DFM, component and EMS vendors, test fixtures, certification, and field reliability. Work shoulder to shoulder with ML and deployment. Your hardware decides what the training data looks like, and you will be on the floor where it is captured. Run contractors and partners without losing ownership of the result. Requirements You have taken at least one product from zero to shipped, with significant ownership of the outcome: as a co-founder, CTO, first hardware hire, or the lead who owned the whole device. Not one subsystem, not one phase. Ideally a wearable, at a tier-one hardware company known for shipping at scale. Electrical engineering is your home discipline. You have designed boards that shipped, across mixed-signal, power, wireless, and high-speed digital, and you can still do it today. You think in systems. You understand how an electrode choice, an enclosure tolerance, and an ADC sample rate interact, and you can hold the mechanical and firmware conversations as a peer, not a customer. You have led engineers: hired them, grown them, and kept a team shipping through 0-to-1 ambiguity. Typically 6+ years in hardware, but we care more about what you shipped than how long it took. A strong understanding of how hardware decisions affect data quality. You know that a great model on a noisy signal still loses to a decent model on a clean one, and you design accordingly. Experience taking hardware to small-batch production: DFM, vendor and EMS management, test, and certification. Genuinely curious about ML: you read papers, you have trained at least one model end to end, and you understand that dataset quality beats model architecture choice. High agency: you don't wait to be told what to do. A 0-to-1 hardware program takes the hours it takes, in person and at pace, and you have chosen that before. Discreet: you handle confidential hardware roadmaps and customer data with care. Nice to Have Wearables, smartwatches, drones, robotics, AR/VR, or defense wearables on your résumé. Camera systems: sensor selection, MIPI and ISP pipelines, and multi-camera synchronization. Low-power and battery design, BLE or Wi-Fi, and antenna integration in small enclosures. Enough mechanical fluency (CAD, tolerances, and materials) to challenge the mechanical team’s choices and be right some of the time. Prior founder or founding-engineer experience, including the parts that went wrong. Open-source hardware or firmware contributions. Who Will Thrive at MicroAGI Everyone we hire is assessed on the same four traits: Mission and vision: you care about what we are building and why it matters, and your past choices show it. Intensity: you work at a pace that matches the size of the opportunity, and you sustain it. Entrepreneurial: you start things nobody asked for, and you finish them. Raw IQ: you learn fast, reason from first principles, and get sharper when the problem changes. This is for you if: You would rather own a problem end to end than wait for a spec. You use AI every day, and you can tell a correct answer from a plausible one. You want to work in person, in the office, with people who are very good at what they do. This is not for you if: You are looking for a predictable 9-to-5. You would forward output you cannot explain. "That’s not my job" feels like a reasonable answer. How We Hire We read every application and reply within five working days. Talent Screen (30 min): a first conversation, both ways. Technical or Functional Interview (60 min): how you think when the problem changes. Your Work (60 min): bring something you are proud of and walk us through it. Leadership (30 min): a conversation with our CEO. Coworking Day (engineering and research roles): a day building with the team on a real problem. Then a decision, usually within a few days. Pay Transparency Compensation includes base salary and equity. The salary range for this role is shown on this posting. What We Offer Agency: real ownership from day one, and decisions that actually matter. Freedom: to choose how you solve the problem, without layers of approval. A seat on a rocketship: one of Europe’s fastest-growing deep-tech companies, at the earliest stage. Free food and drinks in the office. Equal Opportunity MicroAGI welcomes applications from everyone. We assess candidates on their work and potential, regardless of ethnic origin, gender, religion or belief, disability, age, or sexual identity. Powered by physics-based modeling, statistical mechanics, and generative AI, QEMI allows our teams to design novel drug candidates from first principles. What makes AQEMIA different is our commitment to true innovation: our research is dedicated to the invention of new molecular entities, not the refinement of existing ones. We focus on inventing never-before-seen molecules, without relying on experimental data, and advancing them into a growing pipeline of proprietary programs and strategic partnerships with leading pharmaceutical companies. Our most advanced preclinical programs are currently in vivo optimization, targeting diseases still waiting for effective treatments, offering our teams the opportunity to work on science that can make a real difference in people’s lives. For more information, visit AQEMIA.com, our WTTJ Page, and our LinkedIn. About our Team AQEMIA brings together a diverse, multidisciplinary team of 80+ professionals based in Paris and London. Our scientists and engineers, including chemists, physicists, machine learning experts, and software engineers, work side by side to push the boundaries of early-stage drug discovery. This close collaboration across disciplines is central to our approach, enabling us to tackle complex scientific challenges from first principles and translate cutting-edge ideas into novel therapeutic candidates. At AQEMIA, team members are encouraged to contribute their expertise, learn from one another, and play an active role in shaping the future of drug invention. description:
Product Marketing Director

Reports to: Chief Commercial Officer


Location: UK, France, Netherlands, Belgium, Germany, Austria, Spain, Finland, USA. Some travel to our offices will be required from time-to-time

You must have the right to work in one the above countries in order to be considered for the role.

 

💼 About the role

PQShield is looking for a Product Marketing Director who can turn complex technology into stories that people understand, remember, and act on.

You will own how PQShield's products, technology, and vision are positioned, communicated, and brought to market worldwide. You'll sit at the intersection of product, engineering, sales, customers, and the broader security market — translating breakthrough cryptography and security technology into compelling narratives for executives, engineers, partners, and buyers.

This role is for a strategic product marketer and exceptional storyteller who can identify the market shift, understand the customer problem, and turn complex technology into differentiated positioning that creates urgency, preference and demand. 

Since NIST published its first post-quantum cryptography (PQC) standards, which the PQShield team co-authored, organizations across semiconductors, automotive, defense, and enterprise face significant challenges in preparing for the post-quantum transition. This role will help define the market narrative around that transition, position PQShield's portfolio within it and give customers a clear reason to act.

 

⚒️ What you’ll be doing

  • Own the story: Develop the narrative, positioning, messaging, and value propositions that explain what is changing in the market, why customers need to act, the problem PQShield solves, and why our approach is differentiated.
  • Turn technical capability into customer value: Work with cryptographers, engineers and product leaders to understand sophisticated technology, identify what matters to the buyer and translate technical capabilities into clear business and security value without sacrificing technical credibility.
  • Position the portfolio: Own positioning and messaging for our hardware IP and software portfolio, including PQPlatform, PQPerform, PQCryptoLib, and PQMicroLib. Build a clear messaging architecture that connects the portfolio while preserving the differentiated value of each offering.
  • Understand the customer: Develop deep insight into customer problems, buying journeys, security requirements, regulatory pressures, barriers to adoption, buying dynamics, and the forces driving post-quantum adoption. Turn those insights into sharper products, messaging, and go-to-market strategies.
  • Shape category and market narrative: Help define how PQShield talks about post-quantum security, cryptographic agility, and the transition to quantum-safe systems — and how we differentiate our approach in a rapidly evolving market.
  • Lead product launches: Create and execute compelling go-to-market strategies for new products, certifications, partnerships, and major releases.
  • Equip the sales team: Build compelling presentations, stories, solution briefs, case studies, battlecards, and other tools that help sales teams communicate value and win complex deals.
  • Build buyer and segment-specific stories: Develop differentiated narratives for semiconductors, automotive, military and aerospace, industrial IoT, networking, and enterprise, adapting the value story for different buyers, use cases and business priorities.
  • Own competitive storytelling: Understand the competitive landscape and turn technical and commercial differences into clear, credible differentiation.
  • Create exceptional content: Lead the development of white papers, thought leadership, application notes, customer stories, executive content, web experiences, and other material that establishes PQShield as a category leader.
  • Bring customer stories to life: Find and develop the stories that demonstrate why customers are making the transition to post-quantum security and why they choose PQShield.
  • Work across the company: Partner closely with product, engineering, sales, partnerships, and leadership to ensure the market sees one clear, compelling PQShield story.

 

🎯 Required Skills And Qualifications

We're looking for an experienced product marketing leader who is exceptionally strong in positioning, messaging and strategic storytelling. You can take an emerging market, complicated buyer problem or deeply technical product and find the clear narrative inside it.

  • 8+ years of marketing experience, with significant experience in product marketing, technology marketing, B2B marketing, or a closely related discipline.
  • A proven ability to develop positioning and stories that change how markets understand a product, technology, or company.
  • Exceptional written and verbal communication skills. You can take something highly technical and make it understandable, interesting, and compelling without dumbing it down.
  • Strong storytelling instincts and the ability to find the human, business, and strategic narrative inside complex technology.
  • Experience marketing technical B2B products, ideally in cybersecurity, semiconductors, infrastructure, embedded systems, software, or another sophisticated technology market.
  • Strong understanding of security and technology buyers, and the ability to communicate credibly with CISOs, CTOs, engineers, architects, product leaders, and business executives.
  • Demonstrated ability to work closely with technical experts and quickly develop enough subject-matter expertise to challenge assumptions, ask good questions, and tell an accurate story.
  • A strong commercial mindset: you understand that great marketing isn't just about explaining a product — it's about creating differentiation, urgency, preference, and ultimately revenue.
  • Experience launching products and taking complex offerings to market.
  • Experience developing compelling sales narratives and enablement for complex, multi-stakeholder sales.
  • Excellent strategic judgment, with the ability to determine what the market needs to hear, why it matters, and how PQShield should say it.
  • Comfortable operating in a fast-moving environment where you will often need to create the narrative before the market has established one.

 

What we can offer you

  • A competitive compensation package.
  • Share options.
  • A remote first company. You will work from home most of the time, but will need to join us in the office for planning sessions and key meetings as required.
  • Travel for customer meetings and marketing events as needed. 
  • Health insurance.
  • Generous PTO and holiday package.
  • Company contributions towards 401K/pension
  • …and other great benefits.

 

If you enjoy working as part of a technology company, value the security of our daily digital lives, and love solving hard problems - then we’d love to hear from you.

description:
Contexte :

Offre de stage de recherche de master d’une durée de 4 à 6 mois, débutant en hiver 2026-2027. Ce document liste les possibles directions pour le stage, qui seront ajustées au fil du stage. Le stage aura lieu au sein du centre de recherche d’Artefact à Paris.

L’objectif est d'étudier les réseaux de neurones dans un cadre où l’on souhaite garantir l'indépendance des prédictions vis-à-vis d'une variable sensible continue (telle que l'âge, le revenu, la couleur de peau, etc.).

Présentation d’Artefact :

Artefact est une société internationale de services autour de la data, spécialisée dans le conseil en transformation data, dont la mission est de transformer la donnée  en délivrant des résultats tangibles sur l’ensemble de la chaîne de valeur des entreprises. L’approche unique d’Artefact, qui fait le pont entre la donnée et le business, permet à nos clients d’atteindre leurs objectifs business de façon dédiée et efficace. Nos 2500 employés allient leurs compétences pluridisciplinaires au profit  de l’innovation business des entreprises. Nos technologies de pointe en Intelligence Artificielle, nos méthodes agiles garantissent le succès des projets IA de nos clients, de la conception au déploiement, jusqu’à la formation et l’accompagnement au changement.

Sujet :

Les réseaux de neurones sont aujourd'hui au cœur de nombreuses applications industrielles. Leur capacité à extraire des représentations riches à partir des données en fait des outils de choix, mais elle les rend aussi susceptibles d'encoder et d'amplifier des biais présents dans les données d'apprentissage, renforçant ainsi des discriminations chez les populations traitées par ces modèles [1]. Cet enjeu est un domaine de recherche dénommé fairness, et est particulièrement dynamique, avec la réglementation des modèles d’IA qui évolue, comme par exemple avec l’AI Act de l’Union Européenne.


Pour mesurer et mitiger les biais discriminatoires dans les modèles, la littérature s'est majoritairement concentrée sur des variables sensibles binaires ou catégorielles (genre, origine ethnique, etc.), pour lesquelles les groupes sont bien définis [2-5]. Cependant de nombreuses variables sensibles sont intrinsèquement continues : l'âge, le revenu, ou encore la couleur de peau. Discrétiser ces variables en groupes est une pratique courante mais problématique : le choix des seuils est arbitraire, de l'information est perdue, et un modèle peut sembler équitable pour un découpage donné tout en restant fortement biaisé pour un autre [6]. Contrôler la dépendance entre les sorties d'un modèle et une variable continue reste un problème ouvert, notamment pour les réseaux de neurones, où il faut à la fois mesurer cette dépendance et la pénaliser de façon différentiable au cours de l'apprentissage.


Durant ce stage, le/la stagiaire explorera les méthodes de réduction des biais par rapport à une variable sensible continue pour des réseaux de neurones. Le travail commencera par l'implémentation des méthodes existantes (régularisations basées sur des mesures de dépendance telles que la corrélation maximale de Hirschfeld-Gebelein-Rényi ou “Generalized Disparate Impacte”, etc.), listées dans les références [7-8], et par la mise en place d'un protocole robuste pour les comparer, en tenant compte du compromis entre performance et fairness. Dans un second temps, le stage se concentrera sur la conception et l'expérimentation de nouvelles méthodes de réduction de biais adaptées aux variables continues. Pour cela, le/la stagiaire pourra s'appuyer sur des bibliothèques open source (PyTorch, scikit-learn), afin de rester dans un cadre de code reproductible et facile à adopter.

Pré-requis

Le profil recherché pour ce poste est le suivant :
BAC+4/BAC+5 : Formation en mathématiques appliquées, statistiques ou machine learning au sein d’une université ou école d’ingénieur
Stage de césure ou stage de fin d’études
Date de début : Hiver 2026-2027
Durée : 4 à 6 mois

Références

  1. Risser, L., Sanz, A. G., Vincenot, Q., & Loubes, J. M. (2022). Tackling algorithmic bias in neural-network classifiers using wasserstein-2 regularization. Journal of Mathematical Imaging and Vision, 64(6), 672-689.
  2. Buolamwini, J., & Gebru, T. (2018, January). Gender shades: Intersectional accuracy disparities in commercial gender classification. In Conference on fairness, accountability and transparency (pp. 77-91). PMLR.
  3. Cho, J., Zala, A., & Bansal, M. (2023, October). Dall-eval: Probing the reasoning skills and social biases of text-to-image generation models. In 2023 IEEE/CVF International Conference on Computer Vision (ICCV) (pp. 3020-3031). IEEE.
  4. Li, X., Chen, Z., Zhang, J. M., Sarro, F., Zhang, Y., & Liu, X. (2023). Dark-skin individuals are at more risk on the street: Unmasking fairness issues of autonomous driving systems. CoRR abs/2308.02935.
  5. Thong, W., Joniak, P., & Xiang, A. (2023, October). Beyond skin tone: A multidimensional measure of apparent skin color. In 2023 IEEE/CVF International Conference on Computer Vision (ICCV) (pp. 4880-4890). IEEE.
  6. Shilova, V., Malherbe, E., Palma, G., Risser, L., & Loubes, J. M. (2025). Fairness-aware grouping for continuous sensitive variables: Application for debiasing face analysis with respect to skin tone. In ECAI 2025: 28th European Conference on Artificial Intelligence 25-30 October 2025, Bologna, Italy-Including 14th Conference on Prestigious Applications of Intelligent Systems (PAIS 2025) Proceedings (pp. 5344-5351).
  7. Mary, J., Calauzenes, C., & El Karoui, N. (2019, May). Fairness-aware learning for continuous attributes and treatments. In International conference on machine learning(pp. 4382-4391). PMLR.
  8. Giuliani, L., Misino, E., & Lombardi, M. (2023, July). Generalized disparate impact for configurable fairness solutions in ML. In International Conference on Machine Learning (pp. 11443-11458). PMLR.

This is still a young field. The evidence base is growing, best practice is being written in real time, and you will have a genuine hand in shaping it. You do not need experience with cannabis based medicines. You need sound clinical judgement, an open mind and an interest in doing things differently. Highly competitive salary Flexible working with full time or part time options Comprehensive indemnity coverage. description: About ElevenLabs ElevenLabs is an AI research and product company transforming how we interact with technology. We launched in January 2023 with the first human-like AI voice model. Hands-on experience developing agents, with an understanding of prompts, tools, execution logic, evaluations and the challenges of reliable, secure operation. Evidence of independent, end-to-end ownership and confidence working across the stack, including frontend delivery when needed. Good product judgement, clear communication and enthusiasm for creative agents. We may also consider exceptional engineers with closely relevant experience. Familiarity with HTTP, WebSockets and asynchronous workers will help you build reliable communication between services and recover from failures. Experience with multimodal generation, creative editors, MCP, or building products in a small, fast-moving team would be particularly valuable. Right now, the biggest milestone on your plate is the build out of our new AI data centre. You inherit a fully designed Leaf-Spine architecture built on Arista EOS, BGP EVPN, and VXLAN, take ownership of it, refine it where it needs refining, and drive everything from commissioning through to stable production operations. Alongside that, you keep our existing LTG infrastructure running reliably: you design, build, and operate complex network, server, and security systems, analyse and resolve faults, and harden our network security through scrubbers, firewalls, ACLs, and NAC. You monitor network traffic and infrastructure performance, extrapolate the KPIs that matter to management, and coordinate with external service providers and remote hands across the globe. You keep our network diagrams, runbooks, change logs, and system documentation in good shape, and you work closely with Platform Engineering on Cilium BGP peering, Kubernetes node network configuration, and IPAM, acting as the ongoing interface between NetOps and Platform. You join a self-organising, agile team that owns its problems end to end, from analysis to resolution, without micromanagement. On top of that, you will have real room to grow into infrastructure automation, DDoS mitigation with Nokia Deepfield, observability, and BGP EVPN fabric engineering, alongside plenty of national and international project work. You report directly to our Head of Network and become the permanent owner of everything networking related at Contabo Group, Blue and Black alike. What convinces us Your personality, paired with: minimum 5 years of hands-on experience with complex, scalable networks and fabric infrastructures on Cisco and/or Arista, ideally with real Leaf-Spine and BGP EVPN VXLAN exposure strong expertise in WAN connectivity, data centre peering, uplink management, VPN, and IPv6 strong expertise in security administration and DDoS mitigation (e.g. Nokia Deepfield, Aurologic), plus solid monitoring skills with tools like Grafana, Check_MK, or Zabbix good scripting and automation skills with Ansible, Terraform, Python, or similar strong analytical and strategic thinking, paired with clear, confident communication a results-driven, hands-on mindset with a high standard of performance, customer orientation, and composure under pressure genuine team spirit, reliability, and a self-driven way of working that thrives without micromanagement experience with Network Access Control solutions, BGP Flowspec, virtualisation (Proxmox), and IPAM systems such as NetBox strong conflict-handling skills, a knack for building contacts across teams, and openness to change a basic understanding of Kubernetes networking, ideally paired with an Arista certification (or equivalent Cisco knowledge), a completed IT apprenticeship or equivalent, and German language skills alongside excellent English We know that you may not currently meet all the requirements. description: Location: 100% remote (EMEA, CET±2), with team gatherings in person a few times a year Hours: Full-time, 40 hours per week Pay: €60.000 to €90.000 annually, adjusted by experience and location At Miaplaza, we build homeschool platforms that kids aged 4–18 actually want to use — Miacademy, MiaPrep, and our Online High School are serving over 150.000 students today. Our product foundations are strong. What we want next is a step change in how our products feel: more expressive illustration, more purposeful motion, more moments of craft that turn a lesson into something a kid remembers. We're hiring a Senior Product Designer whose craft anchor is illustration and motion. Our design team is small and senior, five designers when you join, and each brings a distinct strength: brand, design systems, research, and now yours The role You'd own product design for the student learning experience end-to-end: from problem framing through delivery, in a Product Trio with a PM and EM who have strong opinions and expect yours. This is product work with real trade-offs — pedagogical, technical, and business — and you're accountable for how it lands, not just how it looks. Beyond Curriculum, you'd set the illustration and motion bar for all of Miaplaza: the standards, motion principles, and character direction that the other designers and the design system build from. A defining part of the role is art-directing AI-assisted production. You'd build the prompts, references, and review process that let a small team produce quality illustration and motion at a scale hand-crafting alone can't reach. We don't expect you to know every current tool — we expect the taste and judgment to direct output rather than accept defaults. You'd report to the Head of UX, with regular 1:1s covering craft, product, and career growth. The direction is upward: deeper craft leadership, cross-product influence, or both. You must have all of these to be considered: A portfolio of shipped digital product work — not only concepts or standalone pieces At least 2 years working as a product designer or a UI/UX designer inside a product team, collaborating with PMs and engineers Strong illustration or motion skills, with at least 1 year focused on either as a primary craft Proficiency in Figma Some experience directing or guiding visual work produced by others — freelancers, junior designers, or AI tools You’ll stand out if you also have: Deep motion skills in product contexts: interactions, transitions, onboarding, character animation Experience using AI image or motion tools as production accelerators Confidence running your own usability research, not just receiving findings Multi-brand or education-focused design experience Accessibility practice, especially for neurodivergent audiences This probably isn’t right for you if: Your work hasn't yet lived inside a live product with real constraints You prefer well-scoped tasks over shaping ambiguous problems You see AI tools as either a threat to craft or a shortcut around it Our hiring process As a remote company, we receive a large number of applicants, and finding the best fit for this role is our top priority — that’s why our process is longer than usual. At every stage, we try to be respectful of your time and grateful you’re spending it with us. Application and eligibility check — work authorization, timezone, availability Async assessment — 12 scenario-based, multiple-choice questions (~30 min) + when qualifying; 3 open questions (max. 45 min) If you pass the multiple choice section, you will asked to complete 3 open written questions (max. 45 min) Portfolio review — the design team will review your best work and thinking Behavioral interview — a conversation with our People team about how you work Take-home design task — ~120 minutes, scoped for this role, AI tools encouraged Hiring team interview — with a design team member and the Head of UX Skip-level conversation — with executive leadership Reference checks We give honest, timely feedback at every step. Job searches are hard; we don't want to make yours harder. Compensation and setup The pay range for this role is €60,000 - 90,000. Miaplaza’s compensation philosophy ensures equity and competitiveness while considering regional differences in labor costs. Placement within a range is determined based on factors such as demonstrated skills, internal equity, and local labor market rates for the candidate’s geographic area. Miaplaza is a growing, self-funded EdTech company. We're an equal opportunity employer and welcome applicants from all backgrounds. If you need accommodations at any point in the process, just let us know. description: About Linro Linro is a cloud security company building a real-time, agentic cloud-security platform. Teams ship with AI. AI ships with Linro. Cloud infrastructure changes constantly, and increasingly it's AI agents making those changes, not people. Most security tools only catch problems after the fact. Linro works differently. We enforce what's allowed at every stage, from commit to production. We stop bad changes before they ship, and fix problems in real time once they're live. We have each been on the receiving end of this problem: running cloud security at scale, building the platforms underneath it, and shipping in regulated systems where a wrong change isn't an option. Founded in Berlin in 2026 and built fully remote across Europe, Linro has a platform that's real and working, with plenty still to shape. The role You will own Linro's security and compliance program end to end, starting from a blank page. Your job is to build that from scratch: figure out where we actually stand, find the gaps, and close them across a multi-cloud environment. Automate what can be automated instead of redoing the same work by hand every quarter. What you will do Take SOC2, ISO 27001 and 42001 from a blank page to audit-ready. Run the gap analysis, document controls and policies, gather and map evidence, track remediation to done, and get us through audit. Automate compliance instead of just babysitting it: build checks and guardrails so we stay continuously compliant, and help ensure our multi-cloud infrastructure (AWS and beyond) is managed as Infrastructure-as-Code with Terraform. Own our compliance evidence end to end: keep it current, mapped, and audit-ready across whatever tooling we run. Support security operations: monitoring, alert triage, and documenting findings. Stay close to how the product is actually built. Our compliance checks run on the same engine we sell customers, so you are testing the product, not filling out paperwork off to the side. What we are looking for Hands-on experience with at least one of SOC 2, ISO 27001, or ISO 42001: you have run a gap analysis, built and mapped evidence, and taken a program through an actual audit, not just studied the framework. Experience across more than one is a plus. Genuine interest in cloud and information security, governance, and compliance, and the drive to own outcomes, not just tasks. Comfort reading cloud configurations and IaC across multiple providers. Ability to automate scales with level. Careful, structured, and trustworthy. You will handle sensitive material. Nice to have Hands-on Terraform, and experience with AWS, GCP, and/or Azure. Exposure to a compliance automation platform. Prior general software engineering experience, ideally in the stacks we use day to day (Go, SQL, and cloud infrastructure) How we work We are remote across Europe and hire anywhere within roughly two hours of Central European Time (CEST). We get the whole team together in person somewhere in Europe once a quarter for a few days. We work async by default, write things down, and protect people's focus time. What we offer Real ownership of the security and compliance program from the ground up. Meaningful equity. You are an early employee, and your stake reflects it. Competitive salary, benchmarked to the market. A quarterly European offsite, and a team that takes both the mission and each other’s time seriously. The honest version This is early, we are literally at the start today. You would start from a blank page, not maintain someone else's polished program. That is the appeal if you want to build a security and compliance function from scratch and carry it all the way to real certifications. It is daunting if you are looking for a mature program to step into. We hire at multiple levels, so this can be a first serious role or a senior mandate. Either way, you will own real outcomes fast. We're now building the AI analyst that takes this work off people's hands - working directly on the customer's own data, scalable without adding headcount. We're well-funded, and we're bringing AI into real estate. Your Mission As a Senior Backend Engineer, you own the systems behind our platform: the GraphQL API, the relational data model, the background processing that turns customer documents and spreadsheets into structured data, and the permission model that lets a single owner and a bank with hundreds of portfolios use the same product. Most of your work runs from schema design all the way to the resolver. You partner with product, design and other engineers to make sure we build what matters - not just what you have been told to do. You take real responsibility for production: when something is slow, you find out why, whether the answer is a bad query, application code or the infrastructure underneath. You also help us make AI reliable in production. Document extraction, long-running analysis jobs and agentic features are core to where the product is going, and we need people who make these workflows testable and dependable rather than impressive in a demo. Our company size of ~40 people ensures that the best idea wins and political discussions are kept aside. And every line of code helps to improve the carbon footprint of real estate properties. From schema design to resolver. Model complex real estate and ESG domains in relational schemas. We run several Postgres databases side by side (one of them geospatial), and schema decisions here have consequences but also positive impact. Own background processing: Excel imports, document extraction, long-running analysis jobs, 3D and image processing. Queues, retries, jobs that spawn other jobs - and figuring out what to do when step 3 of 7 fails at 2am. Develop our permission model. Customers range from a single owner to enterprises with organization/portfolio/building-level access. Integrate LLMs into backend workflows - especially document and data extraction - and make them reliable, verifyable and testable. Debug production. Navigate Grafana dashboards and traces to find out why something is slow or failing, whether in the app, the CI/build pipeline or the infrastructure. Spot overgrown or overly complex parts of the codebase and simplify them without being asked. Paying down complexity is part of the job. What success looks like You have shipped features end-to-end across schema, API and background processing that our customers actively use. Our async processing (imports, extraction, analysis jobs) is measurably more robust: fewer silent failures, clear retry and recovery paths, and observability that tells us what broke and why. You have taken ownership of at least one core area e.g. the permission model, the job orchestration layer or the LLM extraction pipeline and are the person the team goes to for it. You have raised the bar on testing and developer experience in the backend, and other engineers ship faster because of you. You are a trusted sparring partner for product and the team when we decide what to build and how. What it takes You're strong with Postgres. Schema design comes naturally, you can read a query plan, and you know when the ORM is lying to you. Geospatial experience is a bonus, not a requirement. You're fluent in typed backend TypeScript. We work in NestJS and GraphQL every day; if your experience is in a comparable stack, that's fine, you'll pick it up fast. You've built real queue-based processing. You designed workers, dealt with retries and partial failures, orchestrated multi-step workflows. You've designed or worked with authorization for a multi-tenant product and know where it might get hairy. You'd rather have one integration test that hits a real database schema than ten unit tests mocking everything. You write the test that catches the broken migration. You treat production as a debuggable system. You can navigate dashboards and traces to figure out why something is slow, and you don't treat infrastructure as someone else's problem. You communicate clearly - with engineers, product and, when needed, directly with customers. You speak German at C1 level or better and English fluently. Our customers are German banks and asset managers, and you will talk to them. Bonus: AWS (S3, SES, ECS, RDS, …) and IaC. LLMs in production, especially document or data extraction and making it reliable for actual user workflows. Data pipeline work: staged, reproducible processing, dataset versioning. Mentoring or leading engineers, or wanting to grow into it. Debugging tooling and build issues, not just application code. Our toolchain moves fast and is occasionally non-standard. Why Predium? Stage: ~40 people, well-funded, on the way to defining the category. Early enough that a lot still needs to be built. Yes, it's messy sometimes - that's the whole point. At Wolt, we create technology that brings joy, simplicity and earnings to the neighborhoods of the world. In 2014 we started with delivery of restaurant food. The product you will build enforces best practices by design, abstracts database infrastructure, and supports Multi-Region architecture through data sharding and replication. You join a team of highly skilled engineers in designing, building and optimizing this platform and ensuring smooth developer onboarding, constant improvement and optimization. 

As an engineer on the Storage access platform team, you’ll work on platform features such as UI for developer teams, storage abstraction layer, database automation, client SDK and proxy, Change Data Capture pipelines, caching and ephemeral storage, Hot & Cold storage management and more.

Our humble expectations

You’ll be a great fit for this role if you have the following skills and experience:

  • A strong developer-to-developer mindset, with a genuine enjoyment of building for internal customers and treating other engineers as your primary users.
  • Adaptability and strong motivation for working with distributed systems.
  • A data-driven approach to decision-making and a collaborative mindset, with the ability to navigate disagreements constructively and deliver consistently.
  • Autonomy in dynamic, fast-paced environments with frequent change.
  • A product- and platform-oriented approach to engineering challenges.
  • Excellent communication skills, with the ability to engage effectively with stakeholders and cross-functional teams.
  • A collaborative spirit and experience contributing to diverse and inclusive work environments.

Technical proficiencies:

  • Expertise in NoSQL databases, particularly Cassandra or DynamoDB.
  • Experience with large-scale distributed systems, emphasizing both velocity and scalability.
  • Familiarity with SRE principles; however, a background in Backend Development is essential.
  • Practical knowledge of Kubernetes, including EKS, as an end user.

You don’t need to tick every box, but if you see yourself in many of these points, we’d love to hear from you!


What we offer

At Wolt, we’re committed to building an environment where engineers can make an impact while enjoying meaningful challenges. As a member of the the team you’ll enjoy:

  • Working on solutions that support millions of users
  • Solving complex problems in performance, reliability and automation
  • A collaborative and inclusive culture that supports your professional and personal well-being

We also offer flexible work arrangements, competitive compensation, and ongoing learning opportunities to help you thrive.

 

Our Commitment to Diversity and Inclusion

We’re committed to growing and empowering a more inclusive community within our company, industry, and cities. That’s why we hire and cultivate diverse teams of people from all backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives. We believe that true innovation happens when everyone has room at the table and the tools, resources, and opportunity to excel.

description: About AQEMIA AQEMIA is a drug invention company dedicated to creating entirely new medicines to address major unmet medical needs. At the core of our mission is QEMI, our proprietary molecule-invention platform, which uniquely combines cutting-edge science with advanced technology. Powered by physics-based modeling, statistical mechanics, and generative AI, QEMI allows our teams to design novel drug candidates from first principles. What makes AQEMIA different is our commitment to true innovation: our research is dedicated to the invention of new molecular entities, not the refinement of existing ones. We focus on inventing never-before-seen molecules, without relying on experimental data, and advancing them into a growing pipeline of proprietary programs and strategic partnerships with leading pharmaceutical companies. Our most advanced preclinical programs are currently in vivo optimization, targeting diseases still waiting for effective treatments, offering our teams the opportunity to work on science that can make a real difference in people’s lives. For more information, visit AQEMIA.com, our WTTJ Page, and our LinkedIn. About our Team AQEMIA brings together a diverse, multidisciplinary team of 80+ professionals based in Paris and London. Our scientists and engineers, including chemists, physicists, machine learning experts, and software engineers, work side by side to push the boundaries of early-stage drug discovery. This close collaboration across disciplines is central to our approach, enabling us to tackle complex scientific challenges from first principles and translate cutting-edge ideas into novel therapeutic candidates. At AQEMIA, team members are encouraged to contribute their expertise, learn from one another, and play an active role in shaping the future of drug invention. About our Engineering Department The Engineering team (~12 people) builds and scales the technical foundations that power Aqemia’s drug discovery engine. Bringing together expertise across software engineering, cloud infrastructure, data engineering, site reliability engineering (SRE), and scientific computing, the team designs and operates robust, secure, and high-performance platforms that enable Aqemia’s scientific and AI teams to experiment, train, deploy, and run models at scale. Their work spans data infrastructure, scientific compute systems, cloud operations, orchestration, observability, CI/CD, developer tooling, and platform scalability. By transforming cutting-edge research into reliable and scalable systems, the team accelerates the discovery of new medicines while ensuring operational excellence and an outstanding developer experience. The role As our Senior Data Engineer, you'll own AQEMIA's data platform end to end — from ingestion through the pipeline to the trusted, model-ready datasets that power science, ML and analytics. What makes this role distinctive is the data itself: chemical structures, molecular conformations, physics- and ML-based predictions, and experimental results from CROs and partners. A core part of the work is modelling these scientific entities well — establishing canonical identity, provenance and trustworthy lineage across heterogeneous, often messy sources — so scientists, and increasingly AI agents, can rely on them. You'll work at the intersection of software engineering, data infrastructure and scientific research, with real scope to shape architecture rather than just execute against it. As AQEMIA moves toward more service and API-driven integration next year, you'll help make data fit for automation — expanding your impact from pipelines to the systems that consume them. Responsibilities Own AQEMIA's Bronze → Silver → Gold data pipelines end to end, from ingestion through transformation and delivery, maintaining lineage and traceability as data volume and complexity grow. Model canonical scientific entities — compounds, structures, assays, predictions — establishing identity, provenance and trustworthy lineage across heterogeneous and often messy sources. Set and uphold data quality standards through monitoring, validation, testing and alerting across critical pipelines, strengthening governance and observability so datasets stay trusted and accessible. Partner with ML engineers, data scientists and researchers to build curated, model-ready datasets, translating scientific and business requirements into scalable data solutions. Drive data architecture and engineering best practices — data modeling, testing, documentation, orchestration and deployment — in collaboration with the Engineering Manager and Staff Data Engineer on roadmap execution. Build self-service capabilities and, looking ahead, APIs that make data fit for automation as AQEMIA moves toward more service-based integration. Uphold engineering quality through code reviews, and mentor junior engineers by sharing knowledge and best practices as a senior individual contributor. Qualifications Deep experience in data engineering, with a track record of production systems that other teams depend on. We care about what you have built, not the year count. Strong software engineering skills. You code, you review code, and you hold a quality bar. Expert in Python and SQL. - Strong data modelling and relational database experience. You can defend an identity key. Production experience with a cloud warehouse (we use Snowflake) and a transformation framework (we use dbt). Experience with workflow orchestration (we use Airflow) and infrastructure-as-code (we use Terraform on AWS). Any STEM degree or equivalent experience. Nice-to-have Experience with AWS. Experience with infrastructure-as-code (Terraform) and modern data warehousing (e.g. Snowflake, BigQuery, Redshift) and object storage. Experience in drug discovery, biotech, pharma or deeptech environments. Exposure to AI-driven or data-intensive workflows, or experience working across disciplines (e.g. biology ↔ ML ↔ chemistry). Experience implementing data governance, lineage and metadata management solutions. Track record of improving platform scalability, reliability and operational maturity. Our recruitment process First discussion with our Talent Acquisition Hiring Manager’s interview: you’ll meet directly with your future manager Technical assessment of your skills in a deep-dive interview with the team VP interview to share wider team vision and align motivations Cultural fit interview with our co-founder and COO, Emmanuelle Final interview with our co-founder and CEO, Maximillien Why Join Us? At AQEMIA, we work for a mission: joining us means having your own impact on changing the way drugs are discovered, and helping to shape the direction of our fast-growing company and team. Expanding Drug Discovery Pipeline : Focused on critical therapeutic areas like Oncology, CNS, Immuno-inflammation... with in vivo proof of concept/patent stage programs. Collaborations with top Pharma, including a $140M Sanofi deal. World-Class Interdisciplinary Team : work alongside exceptional talent at the intersection of technology and life sciences. Our teams combine deep expertise in AI, physics-based modeling, biology, and medicinal chemistry to push the boundaries of innovation. DeepTech Recognition: AQEMIA is proud to be part of the French Tech 40 and France 2030, highlighting our role as a key player in Europe’s DeepTech ecosystem. Prime Location with Flexibility : Our offices are located in the heart of Paris and London (King’s Cross), with flexible work arrangements including up to two remote days per week. We are 100+ people across London, Palo Alto, and New York, with rapid growth expectations to hundreds. About the Role We are seeking a commercially minded Senior Manager to join Volta's tax function and lead delivery on deals, structuring, and modelling. This role would suit someone looking to move in-house at a fast-scaling, capital-intensive platform. Reporting to the VP of Tax, this is a hands-on delivery role. The Senior Manager will lead deal workstreams, build and stress-test tax models, and monitor governance to ensure tax structures are operating as intended with genuine scope for the remit to grow as the function and business scale. Key Responsibilities Deal Execution & Structuring Lead the day-to-day tax workstream on live transactions - fundraising and capital raises, infrastructure investments and acquisitions, joint ventures, financing and refinancing. Execute the technical analysis and implementation of tax structures agreed with the VP of Tax, across corporate entities, investments/JVs, and debt and equity financing. Review commercial contracts and financing documentation from a tax perspective, flagging issues and options to the VP of Tax. Bring forward clear recommendations on technical questions, with the commercial and risk trade-offs spelled out, for the VP of Tax to decide. Tax Modelling & Commercial Analysis Own the build and maintenance of tax models and supporting schedules for investments, financing structures and transactions. Model cash-tax outcomes and sensitivities, including: Tax depreciation and capital allowances Interest deductibility and financing scenarios Loss utilisation and group relief Withholding taxes, repatriation and transfer-pricing charges VAT and other indirect-tax cash flows Restructuring, refinancing and exit scenarios Feed agreed tax assumptions into the wider financial models, working closely with Finance and Capital Markets. Flag material international tax developments relevant to live deals or models. Governance & Risk Help operate Volta's tax governance framework and controls on a day-to-day basis and keep the tax risk register current. Build and maintain supporting documentation for tax positions, transactions and intercompany arrangements. Manage the working relationship with Big Four and legal advisers on live matters, escalating scope, cost or quality issues. Support tax authority enquiries, audits and ruling applications. Business Partnering Act as the day-to-day tax contact for Finance, Legal, Capital Markets, Corporate Development and Strategy on live workstreams. Give practical, timely tax input on new projects and initiatives, translated into cash flow, returns and capital-efficiency impact. Prepare materials and analysis for the VP of Tax ahead of CFO, leadership, investor and lender conversations. Take ownership of agreed workstreams end-to-end, escalating judgement calls and anything strategically significant to the VP of Tax. Solid technical grounding in international corporate tax – transfer pricing, withholding taxes, permanent establishment and tax-treaty matters. Proven tax-modelling ability, comfortable translating technical rules into cash-flow, valuation and investor-return outputs. Experience coordinating multi-jurisdiction compliance and external advisers. Skills & Attributes Execution-focused and detail-oriented, with good judgement about what to escalate and when. Comfortable owning a workstream end-to-end while operating within a strategy set by someone else. Strong project-management skills, coordinating multiple internal and external stakeholders at once. description: Wir suchen … Dich, als Senior Manager Technical Operations (Bauleiter) (m/w/d), um gemeinsam mit uns bei thermondo einen wichtigen Beitrag zur Klimaneutralität zu leisten. Wenn Du daran Spaß hast Planungs- und Installationsstandard B2B/MFH aufbauen: Entwicklung, Dokumentation und laufende Weiterentwicklung eines verbindlichen technischen Standards für Wärmepumpen-Projekte im Mehrfamilienhaus im Bestand. Dazu gehören Heizlast, Hydraulik inklusive Kaskaden und Pufferspeicher, Trinkwarmwasser und Legionellenschutz, Elektro und Netzanschluss, Schallschutz sowie Aufstellung. Der Standard ist die Grundlage für Planung, Angebotskalkulation und Ausführung durch unsere Installationspartner. Technische Baustellenbegleitung: Prüfung und Freigabe der Planungen und Angebote der Installationspartner, Kick-off vor Ort, regelmäßige Baustellenbesuche und Qualitätskontrollen, Klärung technischer Fragen und Änderungen im Bauablauf. Du bist technische Schnittstelle zu Kunden aus der Wohnungswirtschaft und zu Eigentümern, Partnern, Fachplanern und Netzbetreibern. Abnahmen und Inbetriebnahme verantworten: Durchführung und Dokumentation von Zwischen- und Endabnahmen, einschließlich Inbetriebnahme, hydraulischem Abgleich, Einregulierung und Funktionsprüfung. Du verantwortest das Mängelmanagement bis zur mängelfreien Übergabe an Kunden und Service. Außerdem standardisiert du Abnahme- und Übergabeprotokolle sowie die Nachweisdokumentation für die Förderung nach BEG und KfW. Skalierbare Operations-Prozesse aufbauen: Definition und Implementierung des End-to-End-Prozesses von der technischen Vorprüfung über Planung, Material und Bestellung, Ausführung, Abnahme und Übergabe in den Service. Partner qualifizieren und Qualität sichern: Technisches Onboarding, Schulung und Auditierung der Installationspartner auf den thermondo Standard. Technischen Vertrieb und Angebote unterstützen: Vor-Ort-Begehungen, technische Machbarkeitsprüfung und Konzeptauswahl, zum Beispiel Zentralanlage versus dezentrale Lösung, Kaskade oder Hybrid und Bivalenz. Du plausibilisiert Kalkulationen, Mengen und Aufwandsschätzungen und bist technischer Ansprechpartner für Kunden in der Angebotsphase. Lessons Learned und kontinuierliche Verbesserung: Systematische Auswertung abgeschlossener Projekte hinsichtlich Kosten, Zeit, Qualität und Störungen im Betrieb. Du führst die Erkenntnisse in Standard, Produktportfolio und Kalkulationsgrundlagen zurück. Und Dich hier wiedererkennst Abgeschlossenes Studium, zum Beispiel B.Eng., M.Eng. oder Dipl.-Ing., in Versorgungstechnik, Gebäude- und Energietechnik, Technischer Gebäudeausrüstung, Maschinenbau oder einem vergleichbaren Fach. description:
Shape How the World Discovers Hospitality with OpenTable 

Are you a strategic marketer who thrives at the intersection of high-impact brand media and performance growth? Do you want the agility, ownership, and speed of a tech startup, backed by the scale and resources of a global industry leader?

With millions of diners, 70,000+ restaurant partners and 25+ years of experience, OpenTable, part of Booking Holdings, Inc. (NASDAQ: BKNG), is an industry leader with a passion for helping restaurants thrive. Our world-class technology empowers restaurants to focus on what matters most – their team, their guests, and their bottom line – while enabling diners to discover and book the perfect restaurant for every occasion. 

Every employee at OpenTable has a tangible impact on what we do and how we do it. You’ll also be part of a global team and its portfolio of metasearch brands. Hospitality is all about taking care of others, and it defines our culture.

 A little about the role...

We’re looking for an experienced Senior Marketing Manager to lead upper-funnel brand media and help scale our growth across international markets.

You’ll take strategic ownership of international brand investment, shape channel strategies across Out-of-Home (OOH), Connected TV (CTV) and digital video, and play an important role in defining how we grow and reach diners internationally.

This is a role with plenty of scope to think big, test ideas and get hands-on with making them happen.

Why this role is unique;

  • Startup autonomy, enterprise scale: Build systems, test new channels and move quickly, while having the backing of world-class data, resources and an established global brand.
  • True end-to-end ownership: From building investment cases and managing agency relationships to designing lift studies and getting hands-on with execution, you’ll have real ownership of the outcome.
  • Cross-functional influence: You’ll bring together media agencies, regional market leads, performance marketing, creative partners and adtech engineering teams to make sure everyone is moving in the same direction.
  • Room to grow: As our International Growth practice continues to scale, there’s an opportunity for your remit and leadership responsibilities to grow with it.

📈 What you’ll drive;

  • International Brand Media Strategy: Own the end-to-end strategy, channel selection and investment allocation for upper-funnel activity across key international markets, including OOH, CTV and digital video.
  • Full-Funnel Growth: Connect brand media with performance channels, CRM, organic and social to create a seamless diner journey and maximise ROI.
  • Advanced Brand Measurement: Move beyond last-click attribution by establishing frameworks for lift studies, brand tracking and econometrics to better understand and optimise the impact of international investment.
  • Cross-Functional Growth Systems: Partner with creative and engineering teams to build campaign infrastructure and explore how AI-powered tooling can help us move faster across markets.
  • Executive Leadership Alignment: Turn complex media and growth insights into clear strategies, business cases and roadmaps that help senior leaders make informed decisions.
  • Test, Learn and Scale: Spot opportunities, test ideas quickly, learn from the results and scale what works.

👋 Our ideal candidate...

  • You bring proven experience in integrated, brand or growth marketing, ideally in-house within a consumer tech brand or high-growth international business.
  • You’ve directly planned and executed campaigns across upper-funnel channels, such as OOH, CTV, linear TV or digital video, and understand how to measure their incremental impact.
  • You understand how brand, paid digital, CRM, content and product growth work together, and you’re equally comfortable thinking about the big picture and getting into the detail.
  • You have an owner’s mindset. When you spot an opportunity or something that could work better, you’re comfortable taking the initiative and finding a solution.
  • You know how to scale campaigns across multiple countries or regions and enjoy collaborating across different markets, cultures and time zones.
  • And finally, you love dining. You’re genuinely excited by restaurants, hospitality and the unique energy of dining culture. 🍽️

What we can offer you...

  • 5 weeks paid vacation
  • Private health & dental insurance
  • Work from (almost) anywhere for up to 20 days per year
  • Focus on mental health and well-being:
    • Company-paid therapy sessions through SpringHealth
    • Company-paid subscription to Headspace
    • Annual company-wide week off a year - the whole team fully recharges (and returns without a pile-up of work!)
  • Paid parental leave
  • Time off for your birthday
  • Paid volunteer time
  • Focus on your career growth:
    • Development Dollars
    • Leadership development
    • Access to thousands of on-demand e-learnings
  • Travel Discounts
  • Employee Resource Groups
  • Income protection and life assurance
  • Employee Assistance Program - including 24/7 GP & free legal advice
  • Pension plan contributions
  • Discounted gym membership
  • Bike2Work
  • Season ticket loan
  • Social events & Thursday happy hours
  • Free lunch 2 days per week

The best connections happen face-to-face, whether you’re sitting down to dinner or having coffee with a coworker. That’s why OpenTable has adopted a hybrid workplace model. This role aligns with that approach, with an expectation of coming into the office two days a week—giving employees the best of both worlds: in-person collaboration and flexibility.

Work Environment & Flexibility

At OpenTable, we pride ourselves on fostering a global and dynamic work environment. As a team member with us, you will benefit from a schedule tailored to accommodate a global workforce operating across multiple time zones. While the majority of your responsibilities may align with conventional business hours, there will be instances where you are expected to manage communications - via calls, Slack messages, or emails - outside of regular working hours to effectively collaborate with international colleagues, respond to restaurant partners, and/or address urgent matters. OpenTable will always abide by and consider local laws and regulations.

Inclusion

We’re committed to creating a workplace where everyone feels they belong and can thrive. We know the best ideas come when we bring different voices to the table, so we're building a team as dynamic as the diners and restaurants we serve—and fostering a culture where everyone feels welcome to be themselves.

If you need any reasonable adjustments during the application/interview process, or on the job, we’re here to support you. Please reach out to your recruiter to request any accommodations.
